A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpecBranch study, including corresponding methods, equations, experiments, and Appendices A–G. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite repagination and minor caption clipping in v2.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark measurements in Section 6, accuracy experiments in Appendix D, and additional performance, resource, and sensitivity results in Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark, accuracy, resource, and supplementary experimental results in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same H-RAD predictor, adaptive branch resampling, verification, and posterior drafting procedures. The alternative drafting discussion in v2 G.2 is retained in v3 G.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanEval, GSM8K, CNN/DM, Spec-Bench, and the same resource-constrained scenarios. Multimodal and agentic applications in the new G.2 are prospective directions, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including SpS, AdaEDL, Lookahead, PEARL, and autoregressive decoding where applicable. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same model pairs, sample counts, generation limits, temperatures, metrics, training settings, and GPU configurations. No new evaluation protocol accompanies the future-work discussion.

E4.justification: Component ablations, threshold and feature-layer sensitivity, resource analyses, temperature checks, and feature-history decay results are retained. The memory-constrained experiments and Figure 19 analysis already appear in v2.

E5.justification: Existing uncertainty displays, including Figure 7's latency ± values and shaded plot bands, are retained. Neither version adds or removes seed information, repeated-run counts, or statistical estimation procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Corresponding tables, plots, and reported findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains Deepseek average speedups of 3.23× for SpecBranch and 2.93× for PEARL; no new result entries accompany G.2.

T1.justification: The rollback-latency theorem, truncated-geometric assumptions, Appendix B lemma and proof, and mathematical treatment of drafting and branch sampling are retained without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same branch-parallel and hybrid-drafting contributions, distribution-preservation claim, 1.8–4.5× speedup range, and approximately 50% rollback-reduction claim.

C2.justification: New Appendix G.2 discusses prospective extensions to vision-language/video models, agentic reasoning, and heterogeneous multi-DNN execution. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning rollback, temporal mismatch, and resource constraints remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit repository URL and code-availability statement to the abstract; v2 only promises a later release in Appendix E. Implementation details remain unchanged, and v3 inconsistently retains that future-release sentence.

R1.justification: v3 adds eight references, including DOUBLE, ParallelVLM, Vision-TTT, TALON, and agentic-learning work, in its new future-work discussion. All earlier references and the substantive Section 2 positioning are retained, making this a limited contextual expansion.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short future-work subsection, acknowledgements, and the abstract's code statement, and updates the publication note. Former G.2–G.3 become G.3–G.4 with corresponding cross-reference updates; the existing narrative is otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their content and designs, with limited placement and spacing changes. Figure 19 moves from the bottom of v2 page 28, where its caption is clipped, to v3 page 30, where the complete caption is visible.

improvement.justification: The concrete code-access pointer and fully visible Figure 19 caption modestly improve documentation and usability. Scientific evidence is unchanged. Appendix E's retained promise of a future code release creates an inconsistency that limits the clarity of the reproducibility improvement.
